issue:
While a model is thinking it sometimes opens an inline code span and never closes it, for example this reasoning line:

    Let me use `run_commands to check.

After such a line, a `<tool_call>` that starts a later line of the same paragraph is not recognized: the parser treats it as quoted inline code, the turn ends with reasoning only and no tool call, and the agent waits forever. The same happens when the stray backtick is on an earlier line of the paragraph (`I should check the ls` output first.` then `then run it.` then the call). It must work whether the text arrives whole or in small streamed pieces.

Existing behaviour that must not change: a call inside a fenced code block stays text; a call quoted inside one line of inline code (``The format is `<tool_call>...` and nothing else.``) stays text; and a backtick at the very end of a line (`Use `` followed by the example call on the next line) still opens inline code, so that call stays text.

Some models end short reasoning on a closing quote and give the answer on the same line, with no line break. The raw output

    the user said "Reply with the number only."</think>2

should give the reasoning `the user said "Reply with the number only."` and the answer `2`. Instead the parser decides the model is quoting the `</think>` tag while thinking, keeps everything as reasoning, and the visible answer is empty. The same happens for `it is called 'the tag.'</think>2` and for ``run `ls`</think>2``. It must work whole and streamed in small pieces.

Existing behaviour that must not change: a tag the model quotes inside a pair of quotes or backticks, as in `the tag is "</think>" here` (also with ` or '), is part of the reasoning, not its end.

A tool-call parameter value can itself contain a `<parameter=X>...</parameter>` pair on one line, for example when the model writes a file that documents the call format. When the model then leaves out the value's own closing `</parameter>` and goes straight to `</function>`, or to the next declared parameter, the value is cut at the nested `</parameter>`. This call:

    <tool_call>
    <function=edit_file>
    <parameter=path>
    docs/tools.md
    </parameter>
    <parameter=new_string>
    <parameter=limit>25</parameter>
    </function>
    </tool_call>

should give `edit_file` with `path` = `docs/tools.md` and `new_string` = `<parameter=limit>25</parameter>`, but `new_string` comes out as `<parameter=limit>25` and the rest is lost. Likewise, when `<parameter=old_string>\nx\n</parameter>` follows the nested pair, `new_string` must be `<parameter=limit>25</parameter>` and `old_string` must be `x`. `param_end(text, final=True, name="new_string")` on `<parameter=limit>25</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>` must return the index just after the nested `</parameter>`. It must work whole, streamed in pieces, with streamed tool arguments, and with tool-call recovery on.

Existing behaviour that must not change: a value that has its own closer after a line break (`use\n<parameter=limit>25</parameter>\nhere\n</parameter>`) is read as before (`use\n<parameter=limit>25</parameter>\nhere`), and a second call after the first is not lost.

When a POST handler raises an exception the server does not expect (for example a FileNotFoundError because a cached picture file was deleted under the server, or any RuntimeError), the connection is dropped and the client only sees ECONNRESET. It should get an HTTP 500 JSON error whose `error.message` names the exception: its type and its message, with the traceback in the server log.

Existing behaviour that must not change: a client that went away (ConnectionError, TimeoutError and their subclasses) is still re-raised; when the answer has already begun (`self.answer_started` is true) nothing is sent and the exception propagates; a `BadBody` error still propagates to the caller that handles it; a ValueError still gives its 400.

The live view of the parallel slots (`slots_view()`, used by the Monitor page) shows wrong numbers for a request that started on the solo path and then continued in a slot. Each time a request is admitted to a slot again (with its reply so far), the view restarts its elapsed time and its first-token time, while `generated` counts the whole reply. Right after such a move the view showed `tok_s` of 3,946 for an engine that makes 50 tokens per second, and an `elapsed_s` of a few milliseconds.

Expected: a slot's live view uses the request's own clocks, the same ones the server's per-request status uses: `elapsed_s` since the request began, and `tok_s` as the reply's tokens over the time since the request's first token.

`strata update` refuses with "A model is running, so nothing was changed" (exit 7) when no model is loaded. This happens after the app was closed or crashed with a model loaded: the managed-runtime record is left behind with state "stale" (its owner host is gone), and `updater.serving_now()` counts it as an engine that serves. Loading a model once and unloading it clears the record, which is the only workaround.

Expected: `serving_now()` clears a stale record the way `strata runtime stop` does for a lost host, and leaves it out of its answer. Add a public function `runtime.recover_lost(name) -> dict | None` for this that clears the record of a managed runtime whose owner host is gone, and returns None and touches nothing when the owner is alive (it must never ask a live owner to stop). A record counts as cleared only when the result has `ok` True and `state` "stopped". A record that cannot be cleared (a result that is not ok, a result of None, or an exception from recover_lost) still counts as serving. A record that is not stale (for example state "ready") is never recovered.

Running setup again for an installed model (the desktop app does this when the context-memory option changes) rewrites the run config, and `carry_over(old, cfg)` loses a setting the person made: `STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN=1` in the config's `env` becomes "0". STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN is one of setup's own environment entries and is rewritten on every run, but setup itself only ever writes the value "0" for it (ROCm, resident experts), so a "1" can only be the person's.

Expected: after `carry_over`, an entry of setup's own whose old value is one setup never writes keeps the old value (and `"env STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN"` is in the list carry_over returns). A value setup does write is still refreshed as before: if the old config had STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN "0" and this run writes no STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN, it is not carried over. Other kept settings (other env entries, the drafting mode and its arguments) behave as before.

In a Hyper-V GPU-PV guest (a Windows VM with GPU passthrough), engine detection says the PC needs the CPU engine and refuses the CUDA engine, although `nvidia-smi` in the guest names the card. The guest lists only one display adapter, "Microsoft Virtual Render Driver" with vendor id 1414, so `detect_backend()` skips every vendor's tool probe.

Expected: with only that virtual adapter, detection asks the tools and returns ("cuda", "nvidia-smi") when nvidia-smi answers, or (None, "no GPU tool answered") when no tool answers. Existing behaviour that must not change: a PC whose adapters are only an integrated Radeon (plus or minus the virtual adapter) must not believe nvidia-smi.

On a Windows PC with an AMD card and an NVIDIA card, an AMD setup receives the CUDA 13 engine package, fails its own test start and reports "no ready-made AMD engine". The ready-made engine is fetched by `engine_from_feed()`, which runs `strata update` as a child process; the child detects the GPU again, and that detection takes the NVIDIA card first.

Expected: the GPU family setup already chose travels with the update. Give `engine_from_feed` a keyword argument `backend` ("hip" or "cuda"; empty keeps the old behaviour), passed to the child as the environment variable named by `ec.ENV_BACKEND` (STRATA_ENGINE_BACKEND). The AMD path (`get_prebuilt_hip`) passes "hip"; the standard path (`get_prebuilt`) passes "cuda" wherever it calls engine_from_feed.

With Inkling 2, an assistant prefill (the request's last message is a partial assistant message the model should continue, for example "one, two,") gives content that ends with the literal text `<|end_message|>`, which should never reach the client. Without a prefill the same reply is clean. Example: with thinking off and the prefill "one, two,", an engine reply of ` three` followed by the end-of-message and stop tokens should give the content ` three`, but it gives ` three<|end_message|>`.

Expected: the reply is parsed as text that continues inside the text block the prompt opened, also when the prompt ends with prefill text after the block's opening. A prompt whose text blocks are all closed (an earlier reply in the history ends with `<|end_message|>`) must not count as an open block.

With Inkling 2, `strata_prefix` (a request asks the server for the token length of the prompt's shared prefix, the first N messages) returns almost nothing when thinking is off or the reasoning effort is unknown: a few tokens instead of the whole first message. `Service.resolve_prefix` renders the first messages with the template and takes the common start with the prompt's ids, but the two renderings differ a few tokens in, at the effort line.

Expected: for the first N messages the shared prefix covers the whole of those messages (it ends with the first message's `<|end_message|>`) whatever the request's thinking settings: none given, `reasoning_effort` "low", `enable_thinking` False, or an unknown effort such as "ludicrous".

A server started with `--config <file> --parallel 16` gives the strata-poly engine no `--batch` argument and answers sixteen requests one after another. `main()` reads the run config and puts the saved tuning, `--parallel`, `--batch-groups` and `--split-serve` on it, but then reads the file again through `run_config()` for the first start and keeps only `--gpu` and `--replicas` from the command line.

Expected: the config the engine first starts from has `parallel` (and the other settings put on it above), so the engine gets `--batch 4` for `--parallel 4`, and the service's `cfg_overrides` keep `{"parallel": 4}` so a later model switch keeps it too.

Inside a container with little free memory, `make_room()` drops the page cache of every file named in the engine's arguments before each start. That includes the PLE shard named by `--ple-gguf`, so the engine reads its 26.8 GiB table cold from disk: "PLE table loaded" takes 48-52 s instead of 0-2 s, about 50 s more per start. The table's pages are the very pages the engine maps when `--ple-io` is `ram` or `mmap` (or not given), so keeping them cached adds no memory pressure.

Expected: the PLE shard is left in the cache unless `--ple-io direct` is given (random 4 KiB reads gain nothing from the cache, so it is dropped as before); every other file is dropped as before, and a model with no `--ple-gguf` drops every file as before. A link to the shard (another path to the same file) counts as the shard. Add `ple_table_file(args) -> Path | None` to the module: the Path named by `--ple-gguf` when it is an absolute path and `--ple-io` is ram, mmap or not given; otherwise None.
